description: We are AstroFlame, a team of enthusiastic engineering students from Bangladesh passionate about space science, AI, machine learning, scientific research, and innovative technology. Through FlameExpo, we aim to make NASA's microgravity combustion research data more accessible and meaningful. We welcome curious, creative, and collaborative participants interested in Python, data science, AI/ML, physics, web development, UI/UX, and scientific visualization. Join us to learn, innovate, and explore beyond boundaries!
summary:
FlameExpo: AI-Powered Microgravity Combustion Analysis**

FlameExpo is an interactive scientific data exploration platform developed to make microgravity combustion research more accessible and understandable. Built around NASA's Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) experimental dataset, associated with investigation PSI-25, it transforms complex experimental records into meaningful visual insights.

The platform enables users to explore combustion experiments, examine experimental conditions, compare results, and visualize changes in oxygen, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide measurements. It also provides statistical analysis and correlation exploration to help users investigate relationships among combustion variables.

By bridging the gap between complex scientific datasets and accessible analysis, FlameExpo helps students and researchers explore experimental evidence more efficiently. Our vision is to support further investigation into fire behavior in microgravity and contribute to future research aimed at improving fire safety in human space exploration.

Live Website:https://flame-expo.vercel.app

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/I-Love-You-Oyshi/FlameExpo

Project Details: FlameExpo

AI-Powered Microgravity Combustion Analysis

1. What does FlameExpo do, and how does it work?

FlameExpo is an interactive scientific data exploration platform designed to make microgravity combustion research more accessible, understandable, and easier to investigate.

The platform is built around NASA's Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) experimental dataset, associated with investigation PSI-25. We processed and organized the experimental records into a structured dataset that users can explore through an interactive web interface.

Users can browse and filter experimental records, examine experimental conditions, compare different experiments, and visualize changes in oxygen (O₂), carbon monoxide (CO), and carbon dioxide (CO₂) measurements. The platform also provides statistical analysis and correlation exploration to help users investigate relationships among combustion variables.

2. What are its benefits?

  • Accessible scientific data: Makes complex NASA experimental records easier to explore.
  • Interactive exploration: Allows users to filter, examine, and compare experiments.
  • Visual understanding: Presents combustion measurements through interactive charts and visualizations.
  • Statistical investigation: Helps identify patterns, trends, and relationships within experimental measurements.
  • Research support: Provides a more approachable way for students and researchers to investigate microgravity combustion evidence.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to bridge the gap between complex experimental datasets and accessible scientific investigation. By simplifying data exploration and comparison, FlameExpo aims to help researchers and students formulate better questions and investigate combustion behavior in microgravity.

In the long term, we envision expanding the platform with properly trained and scientifically validated machine-learning models to support more advanced combustion analysis and research relevant to fire safety in human space exploration.

4. What technologies and tools did we use?

Frontend:

  • Next.js
  • React
  • TypeScript
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Recharts

Backend and Data Analysis:

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • Pandas
  • SciPy
  • CSV-based experimental data processing

Development and Deployment:

  • Visual Studio Code
  • Git and GitHub
  • Vercel for frontend deployment
  • Render for backend deployment
